newsitem.title: FRANCE: French shares close lower on dollar, poll fears.
newsitem.headline: French shares close lower on dollar, poll fears.

text.p: French shares closed lower on Friday, ignoring rises on Wall Street and fresh records in London, because of a weaker dollar and unease over a diminishing lead of the government in pre-election opinion polls.

The French market was closed on Thursday when remarks by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan helped bonds and shares and it woke up to a dollar hurt by comments by Japan's "Mr Yen" Eisuke Sakakibara.
An IPSOS poll released on Thursday evening showed a close race between the centre-right and the opposition Socialist and Communist parties ahead of the May 25/June 1 election.

"It's starting to hot up. At the start everybody thought that the right would win, now there are some doubts," a broker said. But analysts said the markets had not yet woken up to the possibility the left could win.
"It astonishes me that they (the market) do not seem to have taken into account that the left could win," Deutsche Bank economist Patrick Mange said.
Others said that the Socialists, if they won power, would probably remain committed to European monetary union in any case.
The CAC-40 index closed down 0.36 percent at 2633.91 and May futures were 9.5 points lower at 2,616. Volume was 5.74 billion francs of which 4.3 billion in blue-chip shares.
"The market is digesting the fall of the dollar and the opinion polls which are not good (for the ruling majority)," a share dealer said.

Traders were reluctant about pronouncing themselves on the market's direction next week, just two weeks from the May 25 and june 1 elections and a few days away from the May 20 meeting of the Federal Reserve policy council.

"There is too much uncertainty about where the market is going. It will very much depend on opinion polls and statements by the one and other in the election campaign," said a broker, adding a continuing U.S. bond rally could support share prices.

The CAC-40 stood at 2,522.67 when President Jacques Chirac called the early parliamentary election on April 21. It rose to a close of 2,651.93 on May 6 before slipping. The index lost 0.8 percent this week.
